device.name: Subaru Impreza / WRX / STi
device.notes:
Subaru uses SSM (Subaru Select Monitor), a proprietary diagnostic protocol layered on top of either ISO 9141-2 K-line (2002–2007) or ISO 15765-4 CAN (2008+). SSM exposes roughly 10× more live data than generic OBD-II Mode 01 PIDs — knock correction, per-cylinder roughness, AVCS cam angles, AF Learning by airflow range, boost error, ethanol content, and hundreds of ECU-internal parameters.
Two transports, one protocol:
K-line (2002–2007) — 4800 baud, 8N1, 5-baud init then SSM framing:
  [0x80, dest, 0xF0, length, COMMAND, payload..., checksum]
  Checksum = Σ bytes (excluding checksum) mod 65536, stored as 1 byte.
  Dest addresses: 0x10=engine, 0x18=transmission, 0x30=ABS.

CAN (2008+) — 500 kbps, 11-bit IDs:
  Request/response IDs are per-ECU and listed in the `ecus` block below
  (engine 0x7E0/0x7E8, transmission 0x7E1/0x7E9, ABS 0x7E3/0x7EB) — the
  standard ISO 15765-4 diagnostic pairs, response = request + 8. Do NOT
  compute them from the K-line dest address: those addresses (0x10, 0x18,
  0x30) are not contiguous, so an earlier "0x7E0 + (dest - 0x10)" formula
  here was wrong — it mapped the transmission onto 0x7E8 (the engine's
  response ID) and the ABS onto 0x800. Payload after the ID is
  [COMMAND, payload...] on request, [RESPONSE, payload...] on reply.
  No SSM header, no checksum — handled by CAN CRC.

The protocol is identical: same commands, same parameter addresses. Only the framing differs. This is the foundation of RomRaider's portability — swap the transport driver, keep the protocol logic.
SOURCE: RomRaider/src/main/java/com/romraider/io/protocol/ssm/ - iso9141/SSMProtocol.java      (K-line transport) - iso9141/SSMChecksumCalculator.java - iso15765/SSMProtocol.java     (CAN transport) - iso15765/SSMResponseProcessor.java - logger/ecu/comms/query/SSMEcuInit.java
DTCs are NOT a separate protocol command. They are regular SSM parameters stored at memory addresses defined in the logger definition XML. Each DTC is a single bit at a (memaddr, bit) location — read that address, check the bit, and if set the DTC is active. Clearing a DTC means writing 0x00 to its memory address. RomRaider defines DTCs via <dtcode> elements with memaddr and bit attributes.

factory_reset.effect: There is nothing to clear. A car reached over its OBD-II connector holds no pairing, credential or client binding — access is physical, and unplugging the adapter ends it. The ECU does hold state a tool can change (learned fuel trims, stored DTCs, flashed calibrations), but clearing any of that is a specific diagnostic operation with its own prerequisites and consequences, not a "factory reset", and it must not be presented as a routine setup step on a vehicle.

methods.description: Plug an adapter into the OBD-II connector and talk SSM over it. There is nothing to provision — the link is physical, so access is granted by being in the car. The one setup condition that matters is the pair of green diagnostic connectors under the dash: leave them DISCONNECTED for reads. Joining them puts the ECU into a mode that accepts flash writes, which is not what you want for reading live data.

steps.action: Locate OBD-II connector under dash, driver's side, above hood release.
Verify green diagnostic connectors are DISCONNECTED (not joined).
Plug in adapter, key ON (engine OFF).
Send ECU init and poll live data via SSM read-address.

setup.notes: Plug in an adapter, key on, send ECU init, read the response. No provisioning, pairing, or credentials. The green diagnostic connectors must be DISCONNECTED for normal reads. Join them for flash writes.

variants.notes: K-line SSM. 5-baud init wakes the ECU. 68HC16Y5 CPU, 192KB ROM.
CAN SSM with extended PID set. FA20/FA24 Denso ECU.

adapter_requirements: CAN: any ELM327 v1.4+ with AT commands and ISO 15765-4 support.
K-line: VAG-COM KKL cable (FT232RL) or Tactrix OpenPort 2.0.
ECU flashing (not covered here): Tactrix OpenPort 2.0 only.

commands.description: Initialize SSM session with ECU. Returns ECU ID + supported-parameter bitmask.
commands.name: ECU_INIT
commands.notes:
K-line: 0x80 0x10 0xF0 0x01 0xBF 0x40 <cs> CAN:    0x7E 0x00 0xAA
K-line response: 0x80 0xF0 0x10 <len> 0xFF <3 unknown> <5 ECU ID bytes> <params_bitmask...> <cs> CAN response:    0x7E 0x80 0xEA <3 unknown> <5 ECU ID bytes> <params_bitmask...>
The ECU ID is 5 bytes starting at offset 3 in the data portion, encoded as hex ASCII. The parameter bitmask starts at offset 8. Each bit represents one parameter (ecubyteindex/ecubit in the logger XML); if set, the ECU supports that parameter.

commands.description: Read parameter values at specific addresses. The workhorse — most tools poll 4–12 addresses per request.
commands.name: READ_ADDRESS
commands.notes:
K-line: 0x80 0x10 0xF0 <len> 0xA8 0x00 <addr1_3bytes> <addr2_3bytes>... <cs>
        0xA8 0x01 for continuous fast-poll (padding byte = 0x01).
CAN:    0x7E 0x00 0xA8 0x00 <addr1_3bytes> <addr2_3bytes>...
Each address is 3 bytes big-endian. The ECU returns all values concatenated in the response. The client knows each parameter's width from the ECU definition (1, 2, or 4 bytes).

commands.description: Bulk memory read — K-line only. NOT SUPPORTED on CAN.
commands.name: READ_MEMORY
commands.notes: K-line: 0x80 0x10 0xF0 <len> 0xA0 0x00 <addr_3bytes> <num_bytes_minus_1> <cs> CAN: throws UnsupportedProtocolException. RomRaider only uses read-address on CAN.

commands.description: Write a single byte value to a 3-byte address.
commands.name: WRITE_ADDRESS
commands.notes:
K-line: 0x80 0x10 0xF0 <len> 0xB8 <addr_3bytes> <value> <cs> CAN:    0x7E 0x00 0xB8 <addr_3bytes> <value>
Used for: ECU reset (address 0x000060, value 0x40), DTC clear (write 0x00 to DTC memory addresses), actuator tests, and tuning parameter writes.

commands.description: Bulk memory write — K-line only. NOT SUPPORTED on CAN.
commands.name: WRITE_MEMORY

commands.description: Soft-reset the ECU. Equivalent to pulling battery for 30 minutes.
commands.name: ECU_RESET
commands.notes: Send WRITE_ADDRESS to 0x000060 with value 0x40. K-line: 0x80 0x10 0xF0 0x05 0xB8 0x00 0x00 0x60 0x40 <cs> CAN:    0x7E 0x00 0xB8 0x00 0x00 0x60 0x40 Response: 0x7E 0x80 0xF8 0x40

connector.location: under dash, driver's side, above hood-release lever

data_identifiers.name: A/F Learning #1 (long-term fuel trim, range A)

requests.description: Begin an SSM session and read ECU identity + supported parameters.
requests.name: ssm_ecu_init

requests.description: Extract ECU ID (CAL ID / ROM revision) from init response. 5 hex bytes at offset 3.
requests.name: ssm_read_ecu_id
requests.notes: The CAL ID is the first 5 data bytes after the 3-byte unknown prefix — e.g. 'A2WC522N'.

requests.description: Read one or more live-data parameters by address.
requests.name: ssm_read_params
requests.notes: Send 3-byte addresses concatenated. Each ROM definition file maps parameter names to addresses and byte widths.

requests.description: Read a single DTC bit at a (memaddr, bit) location. DTCs are regular SSM parameters.
requests.name: ssm_read_dtc
requests.notes: Read the DTC's memaddr via READ_ADDRESS, then check the bit. If 1, the DTC is active.

requests.description: Clear a single DTC by writing 0x00 to its memory address.
requests.name: ssm_clear_dtc
requests.notes: Some ECUs also reset AF Learning when clearing DTCs. Check your ROM revision.

requests.description: Soft-reset ECU — clears learned parameters without clearing DTCs.
requests.name: ssm_ecu_reset

requests.description: Standard OBD-II Mode 01 PID read. Available on CAN models (2008+) alongside SSM.
requests.name: obd2_mode01

requests.description: Standard OBD-II Mode 09 vehicle info (VIN, CAL ID).
requests.name: obd2_mode09

requests.description: Check if a parameter is supported by checking its bit in the init-response bitmask.
requests.name: ssm_check_support
requests.notes: Each parameter in the logger XML has ecubyteindex and ecubit. After ECU init, check byte[ecubyteindex] & (1 << ecubit) — NO bit inversion (RomRaider LoggerDefinitionHandler.isSupportedParameter: (bytes[i] & 1 << ecuBit) > 0). If non-zero, the parameter is supported. This is how RomRaider dynamically adapts to any ROM revision.

connectors.location: under dash near OBD-II port, taped together
under dash near green connectors (2002–2005 only)

transport.notes:
CAN SSM framing (from RomRaider SSMProtocol.java for iso15765): - Request:  [0x7E, 0x00 + offset, COMMAND, payload...] - Response: [0x7E, 0x80 + offset, RESPONSE_CODE, data...] - No header bytes, no checksum — CAN handles framing and CRC.
K-line SSM framing (from SSMProtocol.java for iso9141): - Request:  [0x80, dest, 0xF0, data_len, COMMAND, payload..., checksum] - Response: [0x80, 0xF0, dest, data_len, RESPONSE_CODE, data..., checksum] - Checksum = Σ(all preceding bytes) mod 65536, truncated to 1 byte. - Checksum from SSMChecksumCalculator.java: total - ((total >>> 16) << 16)
The COMMAND byte is the same on both transports. Response codes are COMMAND | 0x40 (e.g., 0xA8 → 0xE8, 0xB8 → 0xF8).
